purpose: Resolve large homogeneous units as aggregate statistical combat actors without materializing ordinary soldiers. This preserves large-battle efficiency while keeping the unit as the only persistent mass-combat organization.
aggregate_state: standard loadout and actual issue state
capability_distribution: Use saved mean/spread/min/max distributions and relevant qualification proportions. Never create one character per ordinary soldier. Named exact/lite actors remain exact and are excluded from anonymous counts where claimed.

contact_resolution.frontage: actual geometry, terrain, order and available bodies determine how many personnel can meaningfully make contact; total unit size alone gives no attack multiplier
contact_resolution.deterministic_sampling: Use registered deterministic randomness/receipt keys when distribution tails or individual contact variation matter; otherwise use analytic expected/distribution mechanics. Persist reproducibility data.
contact_resolution.settlement: Apply casualties, injuries, chakra/resource use, ammunition/tool loss, fatigue and morale/cohesion effects back to the real unit aggregate and named participants.

support: Medical, sensor, barrier, communications and logistics effects are separate support capacities. They do not automatically add line frontage. A support unit explicitly committed to fighting uses its actual troop-type rules and capability.
command: Apply commander effects through data/mechanics/command.json after unit soldier capability is resolved; never add commander physical/skill values to every soldier mean.
vectorization: Materially equivalent units may share one ephemeral calculation for efficiency, but there is no persistent hidden cell/batch. Results are deterministically apportioned back to actual unit IDs and vectorization ends on divergence.
size_invariance: Splitting one otherwise identical unit into children with conserved state does not increase total available bodies, equipment, chakra, frontage, morale, experience or damage. It only changes organization and command burden.
